Body Temperature.severe_value: > 40.0 °C or rapid hypothermia (< 36.0 °C) marking onset of critical phase
Body Temperature.notes: Fever typically lasts 2–7 days, often displaying a saddleback (biphasic) curve. Abrupt defervescence frequently heralds the critical phase.

Platelet Count.severe_value: < 20,000 cells/µL (Spontaneous internal or mucosal hemorrhage risk)
Platelet Count.notes: Progressive drop below 100,000 cells/µL is a cardinal WHO alert sign. Nadir typically occurs between days 4 and 6 of illness.

WBC Count.severe_value: < 1,200 cells/µL or leukocytosis in severe hemorrhage
WBC Count.notes: Leukopenia is one of the earliest laboratory markers of dengue, often preceding the platelet decline. Atypical lymphocytes appear in convalescence.

Hematocrit.notes: A rising hematocrit concurrent with rapidly decreasing platelet count is the most reliable clinical indicator of plasma leakage into serous cavities.

Headache.dengue_value: Severe throbbing frontal headache exacerbated by light
Headache.notes: One of the most frequently reported acute symptoms across adult dengue cohorts.

Retro-orbital Pain.dengue_value: Severe retro-bulbar pain exacerbated by eye movement
Retro-orbital Pain.notes: Pathognomonic hallmark symptom of classical dengue fever.

Muscle and Joint Pain.dengue_value: Excruciating generalized myalgia and arthralgia ('break-bone fever')
Muscle and Joint Pain.notes: Severe musculoskeletal pain predominantly in lumbar spine, knees, and shoulders.

Nausea or Vomiting.dengue_value: Loss of appetite, acute nausea, intermittent vomiting
Nausea or Vomiting.notes: Very common in early febrile phase; progression to >= 3 episodes/day is a warning sign.

Skin Rash.dengue_value: Maculopapular eruption with white islands of normal skin ('islands of white in a sea of red')
Skin Rash.notes: Usually emerges on day 3–5 or during defervescence, may cause mild pruritus.

Severe Abdominal Pain.dengue_value: Severe localized or diffuse continuous abdominal pain
Severe Abdominal Pain.notes: WHO warning sign indicating plasma leakage, gastrointestinal bleeding, or acalculous cholecystitis.

Persistent Vomiting.dengue_value: >= 3 episodes of persistent vomiting in 24 hours
Persistent Vomiting.notes: Critical warning sign necessitating hospital admission for intravenous rehydration.

Mucosal Bleeding.dengue_value: Epistaxis, severe bleeding gums, acute menorrhagia / irregular vaginal bleeding
Mucosal Bleeding.notes: Menorrhagia is a very frequent and distressing mucosal manifestation in women of childbearing age.

Lethargy or Restlessness.dengue_value: Severe prostration, psychomotor agitation, confusion, extreme drowsiness
Lethargy or Restlessness.notes: Key neurological warning sign indicating impending dengue shock syndrome.

Heart Rate.dengue_value: 52-115 bpm (Tachycardia in febrile phase; relative bradycardia during convalescence)
Heart Rate.severe_value: Thready rapid pulse > 125 bpm coinciding with narrow pulse pressure (<= 20 mmHg)
Heart Rate.notes: Relative bradycardia (Faget's sign) is frequently observed in the afebrile convalescent stage. Tachycardia during defervescence signals occult plasma leakage.

Blood Pressure.dengue_value: 90/60 - 115/75 mmHg (Postural hypotension common in critical phase)
Blood Pressure.severe_value: Pulse pressure <= 20 mmHg (e.g. 90/75 mmHg) or undetectable diastolic pressure (DSS)
Blood Pressure.notes: Narrowing pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic <= 20 mmHg) is the primary hallmark of impending Dengue Shock Syndrome (DSS).

AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase).severe_value: > 1,000 U/L (WHO criterion for Severe Dengue with organ impairment)
AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase).notes: Hepatic involvement is common; AST levels are characteristically higher than ALT in acute dengue due to muscle injury and hepatic necrosis.

Serum Albumin.notes: Decline in serum albumin directly correlates with the severity of plasma leakage and serves as a prognostic biomarker for Dengue Shock Syndrome.
